newsitem.title: INDONESIA: FOCUS - Indonesian rupiah, stocks recover marginally.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Indonesian rupiah, stocks recover marginally.

text.p: Indonesian markets staged a marginal recovery on Monday as the crisis in regional currencies eased in the wake of Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's warning against speculation, dealers and brokers said.
They said a gradual recovery in the rupiah currency encouraged investors to revisit the battered stock market.
The rupiah strengthened to a high of 2,565 against the dollar in the early afternoon from 2,610 as offshore investors entered the market and unloaded the U.S. currency.
Money dealers said the rise in the rupiah followed a surge in the ringgit against the U.S. currency after Mahathir's warning of possible action against currency speculators.
Mahathir said on Monday the government would consider taking punitive action against speculators. However, he did not outline what specific measures Malaysia might take.
Although analysts believed draconian measures could be counter-productive to the economy, currencies in the region recovered, with the rupiah breaking the 2,600 resistance level.
"We were driven into the turbulence when the ringgit got hit last week. Now we are experiencing a recovery as the ringgit bounced back on verbal action," one dealer said.
Spot rupiah closed at 2,585/95 in Jakarta, compared with an opening of 2,605/15 on Monday.
It crashed to a historic low of 2,665 against the dollar last Monday after becoming the latest currency to fall victim to speculative attacks which have plagued the region.
The stock market also found support on Monday after sliding last week on the instability in the currency market.
The composite index of the Jakarta Stock Exchange ended up 0.11 percent, or 0.76 points, reversing last week downtrend.
Currency dealers said the market saw the rupiah settling at the 2,550 level in the short-term but added further rupiah strengthening was likely if it could break strong resistance at 2,500.
Trisiladi Supriyanto, vice president of Bank of America in Jakarta, said he expected the rupiah to gradually recover to 2,550 by the end of this week.
"I'm quite confident about the rupiah. It is likely to recover to the 2,550 level by the end of this week."
"Fund managers were already feeling comfortable with the rupiah and started to unload dollars, but they met resistance from local operators," Supriyanto said.
"We saw increased dollar selling by fund managers since Friday. The dollar would have adjusted lower if local operators had supported the downtrend momentum," he said.
The rupiah, which started the year at 2,363 against the dollar, had depreciated almost 10.0 percent by Monday's close.
The rupiah depreciated less than four percent last year.

But economists said it was unlikely that the rupiah could recover to its June level of about 2,430 because the rupiah also needed to be adjusted to weaker regional currencies against the dollar to allow Indonesia remain competitive in its exports.
Daragh Maher, an economist at ING Barings in Singapore, said fundamentals would come back into play once speculative momentum had eased.
But he was uncertain whether the rupiah would eventually revert to an initial year-end forecast of 2,450 rupiah.
"However, what is clear is that fundamentals have not deteriorated to such an extent to warrant the degree of weakness seen in the rupiah during the second half of July," he said.

Maher said a strong balance of payments, robust investment-led GDP growth and a stable debt profile would provide the ammunition for fundamental players to re-enter the market once the current wave of speculative momentum dissipated.
